is_benchmark.description:
True for deployments created by the benchmark suite (model_name prefixed
"benchmark-", see scripts/benchmarks/scenarios.py) - lets the dashboard tell
them apart from real deployments without a DB column, since it's fully
derivable from a field already on the row.
is_benchmark.title: Is Benchmark

GatewayOut.description:
GET /router/gateway, passed through. `reachable` false means the router
didn't answer, and `policy`/`models` are empty.
GatewayOut.title: GatewayOut

GatewayOutcomes.description:
Requests in the rolling window by how they ended. `gateway_error`: the
version couldn't be reached or wasn't ready; `rejected`: its circuit
breaker was open, so the router answered 503 without trying.
GatewayOutcomes.title: GatewayOutcomes

LabelIn.description:
One ground-truth label - what a label feeder POSTs to /api/labels[/batch].
`prediction_id` is the join key back to a specific PredictionMetric - see
GroundTruthLabel and label_service.py.
LabelIn.title: LabelIn

LabelReportItem.description:
Per-item result, returned by both POST /api/labels (a list of one) and
POST /api/labels/batch (the whole batch) - the same shape either way, so a
caller never needs two different response parsers.
LabelReportItem.title: LabelReportItem

LoadTestResultOut.description:
Mirrors scripts/benchmarks/report.py's LoadTestResult (what the benchmark
subprocess writes); declared here so the API schema is exact.
LoadTestResultOut.title: LoadTestResultOut

MetricIn.description:
What the router POSTs after each forward. Kept small on purpose - this is the
hot path.

Deliberately has no `actual_label` field: ground truth is never known at
prediction time, so this endpoint must never accept it directly from a
caller - it's only ever written to GroundTruthLabel, via POST /api/labels
(see label_service.ingest_label) and joined against PredictionMetric at
read time (see metrics_service.compute_version_summary). See
docs/DESIGN_NOTES.md.
MetricIn.title: MetricIn

MetricsBucket.description: One time bucket of PredictionMetric rows for one version.
MetricsBucket.title: MetricsBucket

ObservedModelConfig.description: One model's split as the router itself reports it.
ObservedModelConfig.title: ObservedModelConfig

PolicyConfig-Input.description:
A named set of promotion-gate thresholds for one evaluation run.

`evaluation_window_seconds` is part of the policy definition itself, not a
caller-supplied query parameter (unlike the comparison endpoint's
`window_seconds`) - a policy's outcome should be reproducible from the policy
alone, not depend on whatever window a client happened to pass that call.
PolicyConfig-Input.title: PolicyConfig

PolicyConfig-Output.description:
A named set of promotion-gate thresholds for one evaluation run.

`evaluation_window_seconds` is part of the policy definition itself, not a
caller-supplied query parameter (unlike the comparison endpoint's
`window_seconds`) - a policy's outcome should be reproducible from the policy
alone, not depend on whatever window a client happened to pass that call.
PolicyConfig-Output.title: PolicyConfig

RouterConfigOut.description: One model's authoritative split, as the router's startup sync reads it.
RouterConfigOut.title: RouterConfigOut

TimelineEventItem.description:
One DeploymentEvent row, tagged for the merged timeline (see
app/control_plane/timeline.py).
TimelineEventItem.title: TimelineEventItem

TimelinePolicyItem.description:
One PolicyEvaluation row, tagged for the merged timeline, plus a derived
human-readable `explanation` (see app/policy/explain.py) - the raw
observed_value/threshold/result alone don't say *why* e.g. minimum_requests
stayed INCONCLUSIVE.
TimelinePolicyItem.title: TimelinePolicyItem

post.description:
Starts a benchmark scenario as a background subprocess and returns
immediately with status=RUNNING - poll GET /api/benchmarks/current or
GET /api/benchmarks/{run_id} for progress. 409 if one is already in flight: the
router has a single active traffic split, so two concurrent runs would silently
fight over it rather than fail loudly.

schema.title: Response Get Scenarios Api Benchmarks Scenarios Get
Response List Deployments Api Deployments Get

post.description:
Used exclusively by the automated worker (app/worker/) to move the canary to
the next traffic stage after a PASS evaluation. Rejects (409) if the deployment
isn't CANARY_RUNNING/EVALUATING (e.g. a human already acted on it) or if the
canary is already at the last traffic stage (use /promote instead).

Run the policy engine against this deployment's current comparison window and
record each check as a PolicyEvaluation row. Does not change deployment.status -
promote/rollback/advance-traffic/record-inconclusive are separate calls (made by
the worker or a human); this just evaluates and reports. An optional PolicyConfig
body overrides the deployment's own persisted policy_config for this one call
only (nothing is re-saved).

409s if the deployment isn't CANARY_RUNNING or EVALUATING - a terminal
deployment (PROMOTED/ROLLED_BACK/FAILED/INCONCLUSIVE) has nothing left to
evaluate, and writing more PolicyEvaluation rows against it would just pollute
its timeline with checks that can no longer affect anything.

Hot path: the router calls this once per forwarded /predict, fire-and-forget.

Deliberately minimal - a single PK existence check (no relationship loading, no
join) plus a plain insert. No state-machine involvement, no event logging.

get.description:
Latency and error rate over time, stable vs canary, bucketed. Covers the
whole rollout (start to decision, or to now while live) unless window_seconds
narrows it to the most recent part.

post.description:
Stops the automated worker from touching this deployment - see
Deployment.automation_paused and docs/DESIGN_NOTES.md#manual-automation-hold.
Manual /evaluate, /promote, /rollback are unaffected. 409 if the deployment is
already terminal (nothing left to pause).

post.description:
Used exclusively by the automated worker when an evaluation comes back
INCONCLUSIVE: bumps the retry counter and freezes the deployment into
INCONCLUSIVE status once policy_config.max_inconclusive_retries is exceeded.

Lets the automated worker act on this deployment again. 409 if the
deployment is already terminal.

"conflict"), so a feeder sending a mixed batch gets a full report instead of
the whole batch aborting on the first problem row.

get.description:
The thresholds a new deployment gets when it doesn't send its own
policy_config (environment-configurable, see PolicySettings) - what the
dashboard's rollout form starts from.

The router's startup-sync source: every model's authoritative traffic
allocation (see get_router_config below for what "authoritative" means).
Deliberately without revision, same as the single-model form: the router
boots with the right split, and the reconciler stamps the revision on its
next tick.

schema.title: Response List Router Configs Api Router Config Get

get.description:
The authoritative traffic allocation for one model (see
service.get_authoritative_allocation - the active rollout if one is in
flight, otherwise the most recent PROMOTED/ROLLED_BACK deployment's final
allocation), so a restarted router doesn't boot with a stale default split -
including after a rollout has already *finished*. See
docs/DESIGN_NOTES.md#desired-observed-reconciliation.

Deliberately minimal - a plain GET, no push/webhook, no polling loop. The control
plane remains the source of truth; the router just reads it once at startup.

Read-only passthrough of the router's live gateway view - what the
dashboard's flow page animates from. Like /observed, `reachable` tells a
router that's down apart from one with no traffic.

Read-only passthrough of every model's observed split on the router (GET
/router/configs) - never mutates anything, unlike POST /reconcile. Exists so
the dashboard (which only ever talks to the control plane, not the router
directly) can show desired-vs-observed drift without triggering a
correction just by loading a page.

`reachable` is the field the dashboard must check first: a router that's
down and one that's up but doesn't hold a split for some model both leave
that model out of `configs`, so only whether the GET itself succeeded can
tell them apart. See docs/DESIGN_NOTES.md#desired-observed-reconciliation.

post.description:
Compares the router's observed (deployment_id, revision) for every model
against the DB's desired state and re-pushes where they differ - see
app/control_plane/reconcile.py and
docs/DESIGN_NOTES.md#desired-observed-reconciliation. Called once per sweep by
the worker's poll loop (app/worker/loop.py); never raises on its own account -
a genuinely unreachable router or "nothing to reconcile" are both reported as
`reconciled: false` with a `reason`, not an error.

The top-level fields summarise the sweep (the first correction made, if any);
`models` has one entry per model checked.

get.description:
Server-Sent Events: one `change` event per new DeploymentEvent or
PolicyEvaluation row (see app/control_plane/feed.py). The dashboard uses it to
refetch exactly what changed instead of polling every few seconds.
